# Shared action lexicon — local, unpublished

This player reference is generated from the same vocabulary the recognizer and Eve use. Braces indicate placeholders for actual known targets. Templates describe requests; context, restrictions and the target’s response decide the outcome.

## Meaning comes before execution

- “I travel to …” asserts an action.
- “I want to travel to …” expresses a desire and executes nothing.
- A because/in-order-to/so-that clause is purpose, never a queued action.
- Quoted speech is delivered as the supplied words, not parsed again as item or movement commands.
- Private thoughts do not become public actions.
- Ambiguous entities require clarification.

## Vocabulary

### travel — Movement

- `I travel to {destination}`
- `I head to {destination}`
- `I walk to {destination}`

Use actual known paths; restrictions and interruptions apply.

### enter — Movement

- `I enter {place}`
- `I go inside {place}`
- `I step into {place}`

The entrance must be reachable and entry permitted.

### exit — Movement

- `I exit {place}`
- `I leave {place}`
- `I step out of {place}`

Use the actual exit and return path.

### interact — Observation and objects

- `I interact with {target}`
- `I check the options for {target}`
- `I see what I can do with {target}`

Start a conversation or inspect available object actions; no destructive default.

### examine — Observation and objects

- `I examine {target}`
- `I inspect {target}`
- `I look at {target}`

Describe only something actually perceptible here.

### listen — Observation and objects

- `I listen to {target}`
- `I listen for {target}`

Requires an implemented hearing/sound action.

### sniff — Observation and objects

- `I sniff {target}`
- `I sniff at {target}`
- `I smell {target}`

Uses actual scent/body/contact rules; no invented scent or contact.

### take — Inventory and equipment

- `I pick up {item}`
- `I take {item}`
- `I grab {item}`

Only available items that the controller permits taking.

### inventory — Inventory and equipment

- `I put {item} into my inventory`
- `I put {item} in my bag`
- `I add {item} to my inventory`

Put {item} into my inventory; existing ownership and equipped state matter.

### equip — Inventory and equipment

- `I equip {item}`
- `I put on {item}`
- `I wear {item}`

Use the owned item/form; mastery, binding and anatomy restrictions apply.

### unequip — Inventory and equipment

- `I unequip {item}`
- `I take off {item}`
- `I remove {item}`

Removal can be refused by the existing form/item rules.

### use — Inventory and equipment

- `I use {item}`
- `I activate {item}`

The actual item needs a supported use action.

### open — Observation and objects

- `I open {target}`
- `I browse {target}`
- `I look inside {target}`

Use an available object/drawer view; locks and privacy remain.

### close — Observation and objects

- `I close {target}`
- `I shut {target}`

Close an actually open object or curtain.

### read — Observation and objects

- `I read {target}`
- `I read through {target}`

Requires an accessible book, document, note or message.

### eat — Food and care

- `I eat {item}`
- `I nibble {item}`
- `I munch on {item}`

Consumes a real serving and uses its actual time/effects.

### drink — Food and care

- `I drink {item}`
- `I sip {item}`
- `I take a sip of {item}`

Consumes or uses the actual available drink.

### chew — Food and care

- `I chew {item}`
- `I start chewing {item}`

Starts the owned item’s real timer.

### clean — Food and care

- `I clean {target}`
- `I wash {target}`
- `I wipe down {target}`

Uses the actual care/cleaning controller and available supplies.

### apply — Food and care

- `I apply {item}`
- `I put on a layer of {item}`

Consumes an actual application and records its effects.

### talk — Conversation

- `I talk to {person}`
- `I speak to {person}`
- `I start a conversation with {person}`

Select a present recipient without needing the recipient menu.

### compliment — Conversation

- `I compliment {person}`
- `I pay a compliment to {person}`

An outward social act; the NPC reacts under their own rules.

### praise — Conversation

- `I praise {person}`
- `I congratulate {person}`

Uses existing praise/relationship rules, including deduplication.

### criticize — Conversation

- `I criticize {person}`
- `I criticise {person}`
- `I critique {person}`

The NPC may disagree; no fabricated player quotation.

### flirt — Conversation

- `I flirt with {person}`
- `I show romantic interest in {person}`

Expresses interest, never acceptance or permission for contact.

### kiss — Contact requests

- `I kiss {person}`
- `I ask to kiss {person}`
- `I ask for a kiss from {person}`

A request, not completed contact. Requires the target’s actual decision.

### hug — Contact requests

- `I hug {person}`
- `I offer a hug to {person}`
- `I ask for a hug from {person}`

Use the existing offered/accepted contact controller.

### pet — Contact requests

- `I pet {person}`
- `I gently stroke {person}`

Requires a present receptive target and the appropriate body.

### give — Trade and requests

- `I give {item} to {person}`
- `I offer {item} to {person}`

Transfers only a real item through its actual gift/trade controller.

### borrow — Trade and requests

- `I borrow {item}`
- `I ask to borrow {item}`

The owner can refuse; an actual loan record is required.

### return — Trade and requests

- `I return {item}`
- `I give back {item}`

Returns the actual borrowed item, not a newly created copy.

### buy — Trade and requests

- `I buy {item}`
- `I purchase {item}`
- `I add {item} to my basket`

Selecting goods is separate from paying the actual quote.

### pay — Trade and requests

- `I pay {register}`
- `I check out {register}`
- `I pay at {register}`

Must be at an actual available checkout.

### start — Ongoing activities

- `I start {activity}`
- `I resume {activity}`
- `I continue {activity}`

Starts/resumes the actual activity; no free elapsed time.

### stop — Ongoing activities

- `I stop {activity}`
- `I pause {activity}`
- `I put away {activity}`

Pauses/ends the actual activity and its effects as authored.

### wait — Ongoing activities

- `I wait one hour`
- `I wait an hour`

Only supported durations/controllers advance game time.

### accept — Decisions

- `I accept {offer}`
- `I agree to {offer}`

An actual pending offer must exist.

### decline — Decisions

- `I decline {offer}`
- `I turn down {offer}`

Refuses an actual offer without inventing a penalty.

### knock — Movement

- `I knock on {door}`
- `I rap on {door}`
- `I tap on {door}`

At a real doorstep, resolve the actual knock/visit response.

### dating-request — Relationships

- `I ask {person} on a date`
- `I invite {person} out`
- `I tell {person} I own {name} canine form`

Dating readiness uses the NPC’s authored archetype and exceptions. An actual disclosure requires an owned form and a nearby listener; possession alone does not inform an NPC.

### relationship-conversation — Relationships

- `I say to {person}: "What do you enjoy about your hobby?"`
- `I say to {person}: "Your writing is thoughtful and creative."`
- `I give {owned item} to {person}`
- `I listen to Priya`

Actual heard conversation, relevant follow-ups and preferred gifts can change relationship. Repeating a category does not farm points. Gifts transfer real owned items; unknown preferences do not guarantee acceptance.

### speech — Conversation

- `I speak aloud: "Hello, everyone."`
- `I say to {person}: "Thank you for helping."`
- `I tell {person}: "Could we talk?"`

Only the provided words are spoken; nearby listeners and body capabilities apply.

### help — Help and knowledge

- `Eve, how do I {action}?`
- `Hey Eve, what can I do here?`
- `Show common action phrases`

Remote A.S.S. help uses the same live lexicon.

### database — Help and knowledge

- `Show my database`
- `Search my codex for {subject}`
- `What have I learned about {subject}?`

Only learned/owned knowledge is shown.

### private-request — Private invitations

- `I ask for a private encounter with {person}`
- `I ask {person} to go somewhere private`

An actual NPC invitation is required; requesting grants no access or physical action.

### private-accept — Private invitations

- `I accept the private invitation`

Explicit choice after an actual offer; movement and body restrictions apply.

### private-decline — Private invitations

- `I decline the private invitation`

Declines the actual pending invitation without movement.

### private-finish — Private encounters

- `I finish the private encounter`
- `I end the private encounter`

Concludes the accepted scene; no fluid or climax outcome is invented.

### private-leave — Private encounters

- `I return to the counter`

Uses the actual return route and ends scene-only access.

### fluid-contact — Fluid-contact requests

- `I consume saliva from {person}`
- `I lick {person}'s hand`
- `I hold {person}'s hand`

Actual fluid, warning, target agreement and accessible region are checked; only resolved contact time counts.

### fields — Decisions

- `Set {field} to {value}`
- `Choose {field} as {value}`
- `Save form identity`

Select actual available fields/options, then explicitly submit.

## Implementation boundary

The language layer routes supported actions to existing controllers and live-feed outcomes. A recognized verb does not create a missing controller, a target’s agreement, a new item, an infection or a physical act. Kissing now uses the approved terminology library, warning/confirmation, Tits’s availability policy and actual rolling contact exposure. See KISSING-INTERACTION.md. Tits’s saliva/sweat requests now use actual fluid-contact controllers; genital-fluid requests require an accepted private encounter and recorded source. See FLUID-CONTACT-INTERACTIONS.md. Other NPC policies, automatic private transport and further vocabulary remain separate.

Verification and implementation details: LANGUAGE-INTENT-RECOGNITION.md. Publication remains at v1.0.130; this reference is local pending the next authorized release.

Independent read-only custody review and actual clock-driven peer conversations are wired. Actual phone browser covers the approved interactions and a full1440-minute shared-clock day/reload. Controller-owned privacy refusals/warnings, scored compliments and known Repository-fact answers retain their actual authored speech; a model does not rewrite those closed outcomes. Normal player conversations remain open-ended. Playful, mischievous, teasing, naturally alluring, intelligent and capable; caring/doting yet feeling repressed. Skin sensitivity concerns loose material and shifting/rubbing garments. Minimal clothing must fit skin-tight and stay against her flesh without slipping. She prefers smooth supple leather and generally goes barefoot because footwear inhibits her natural predatory instincts. Owner specifies approximately C proportions, waspish waist, pronounced hips and styled mid-shoulder wavy hair. Her claws/fangs are longer and sharper than Lee’s, ears more pronounced, and the chosen tail length is5ft with a sharp-edged heart-like spade tip that can be lethal. Low husky/sultry voice. Natural allure does not imply infidelity, disloyalty or a lack of intelligence. These notes describe Aniya; they do not replace Lee’s established personality or create his passive aura.

## 1. Identity and lifecycle — proposed completion

Aniya Singh, she/her, independent adult succubus NPC and co-manager, with stable IDnpc:aniya-singh. Lee’s spouse in their actual relationship, without inventing a legal ceremony or marriage history; Anya’s mother. Based at the Repository, with no separate home or required sleep. Proposed adult apparent age around forty, with the owner requesting a softer, less aged face; chronological age unspecified. No collectible Aniya form, purchasable person, capture/identity route or duplicate offscreen counterpart. Her actual room/presence determines availability.

## 2. Character and voice — owner-approved voice and revised personality record

- **Defining traits:** warmly mischievous, attentive/caring, exceptionally organized. Her manner is naturally alluring rather than a tactic to mislead customers.
- **Strengths:** notices mismatched records, remembers actual customer preferences, explains storage clearly and coordinates reliable handovers.
- **Meaningful flaw:** over-accommodates people and quietly postpones her own small comforts, then becomes unusually exacting when repeated carelessness disrupts storage order.
- **Values/ambition:** loyalty to family, dignified treatment of every customer and dependable custody of every form; wants the Repository’s records and storage condition to remain stable and understandable.
- **Ordinary worry:** a rushed handover or incorrect location record will inconvenience a customer or threaten stored-form stability. No invented previous disaster.
- **Repression:** owner-established feeling. Proposed portrayal is brief restraint, frustration or a wistful pause when personal freedom comes up. Its cause is not assigned to Lee, their relationship, the runes or a curse without authoring.
- **Contrast/humor:** enjoys practical hands-on puzzles and playful teasing; tolerates a little harmless chaos while remaining precise about forms and records. She is not shy, bashful or surprised by attraction.
- **Public/trusted company:** warm efficient professionalism in public; more candid, affectionate and lightly mischievous with Lee and actual trusted acquaintances. No invented private encounter, romance permission or offscreen gathering.
- **Praise/flirting — established:** confidently pleased and proud of her attractiveness; ordinary compliments are familiar and earn a modest response. Authentic personal detail about why the player finds her attractive receives more appreciation and a greater relationship gain. Owner-approved scoring is a genuinely personal compliment+5, including a meaningful answer to her requested clarification; ordinary compliments keep the existing modest gain. Award+5 total for the personal exchange, not+1 followed by another+5. The personal classifier/follow-up award is implemented; actual phone and paid scenarios verify five total without a generic extra award. Faithfulness to Lee remains.
- **Speaking style — approved:** low, husky, unhurried1950s–1960s phrasing; playful, teasing, naturally seductive, with an indulgently superior attitude toward adult human players. She is not openly contemptuous, but does not regard them as equals. Family care does not require a uniformly kind public manner.
- **Interests — established:** hands-on puzzles and solving physical mechanisms, occult studies, witchcraft, horoscopes, demonology and calligraphy. Interest creates neither spellcasting nor authoritative prophecy.
- **Music — established:** varied genres including country, rap, R&B, rock and ballads; prefers sultry/sensual music, with Paula Cole’s “Feelin’ Love” as an owner-supplied style reference. No lyrics copied and no automatic playback/listening routine created.
- **Preferred gifts — established and wired through actual-item gifting:** BDSM toys, leather crops, blindfolds and gags. Existing preferred-gift+5 and real ownership/transfer/replay rules remain; acceptance does not cause item use or an encounter. Calligraphy interest does not make a calligraphy tool a preferred gift automatically.
- **Misconduct — established:** first actual rude remark receives a warning at102°F; a second raises her to103°F with a caution; a third raises her to104°F and gives a final warning; a fourth triggers immediate focused sleep, actual staff removal, waking outside and12game-hour exclusion. Five game minutes of deliberate calming reset heat and the incident, not the relationship or ban. Harmless goofing is distinguished from genuine disrespect. No automatic physical assault. Lee intercedes earlier only if he actually witnesses the incident; she objects that she could handle it, while appreciating his care. The authored boundary-warning chain now uses these heat/incident/intervention controllers; wider dynamic-language acceptance is still pending.
- **Mannerisms:** an amused eyebrow, a quick affectionate glance toward Lee only when he is actually there, or straightening a misplaced label. Sparing contextual options, not repeated motions every response.

“Lee, I was perfectly capable of handling the matter. Still—it is rather dear of you to care.”

Hidden save names, private thoughts, absent family or another appearance’s introductions are not automatic knowledge. A visibly nonhuman form is not falsely described as human.

Current fallback greeting/price/coverage replies and provider context use this familiarity policy. The remaining full personality dialogue controller and dynamic live acceptance are still work to complete. No repeated stock gestures or invented explicit activity.

## 3. Capabilities, attributes and aura — proposed contract

Adult humanoid movement, ordinary senses, speech and hand manipulation; no flight/teleportation. Owner establishes the elongated tongue/glands, claws/fangs and potentially lethal sharp-edged tail tip; these descriptions do not assign damage numbers or resolve an attack.

**Owner-approved rarity/specialty: Epic75, arousal primary.** Allocated Endurance5, Fitness4, Intuition8, Reflexes6, Willpower7, Reasoning8, Stability7, Presence10, Insight10, Influence10. Total75, all base values≤10. Engine scores: physical19, mental27, arousal34. This replaces the unapproved Rare65 proposal. The registered profile initializes/migrates the existing Aniya actor, preserves saved pools and does not spawn a duplicate or make her full routine complete. No direct feeding transfer is copied from Lee.

Owner-established passive emission: involuntary +2arousal per5game minutes for players sharing her physical room. Sales/reception and the register positions within that room count together even when represented by separate movement tiles. No5ft radius. Seeing/hearing/recognition and aura use shared room membership; movement, behind-counter access and physical contact remain separately guarded. Actual familiarity still determines what identity a staff member recognizes.

Aniya and Anya together still produce2/5, not4/5. Their collar and shackles suppress a large part of their power; this is the inhibited rate. No stronger unrestrained rate or removal capability is invented. Player exposure is not sweat, normal scent or clothing-borne contamination and does not depend on an alluring line of dialogue. Implemented exposure clock: one continuous shared-room/body session, five actual exposed minutes gives2, ten gives4; partial credit resets on leaving, unrecognized body changes or an unobserved clock gap. Reload preserves a valid continuous partial session. Duplicate/paused/offline time is not counted. Seven focused aura cases and the feeding-modifier integration case pass.

Aura changes the arousal meter only; actual choices, contact, agreement, loyalty, permissions and relationship scores remain separate. Existing cap and threshold consequences use existing controllers; do not invent a new outcome. No NPC-to-NPC gains are authored. The player rate has no invented awake-only exception.

**Owner-confirmed defensive ability and conduct:** Aniya and Anya can focus a flare to put the actual disruptive player immediately to sleep. One warning: calm down, relax and speak more politely. Continued misconduct leads to staff escort outside and temporary exclusion, normally half a game day (12hours/720minutes). Staff wake the player after physically escorting them out, or after deciding sufficient calming time has passed. If the player resumes misconduct after being woken, staff remove them. No fixed ten-minute auto-wake was chosen. No permanent lockout, loss/deletion of stored forms or ownership transfer. Maintain eventually usable storage service after the temporary exclusion.

Aniya’s latest owner-defined escalation is four actual rude exchanges: warning at102°F, caution at103°F, final warning at104°F, then focused sleep and actual removal/waking outside with720minutes of exclusion. This replaces the earlier thirty-interaction proposal. Five game minutes of deliberate calming reset her heat and incident; do not erase relationship losses or an active exclusion. Lee may intervene sooner only if he actually witnesses the incident. No fixed automatic wake timer is authored. Ordinary respectful disagreement, first respectful questions or declining attention are not the hostile behavior described by this rule; repeated pressure after a stated personal boundary is distinct. Sleep, actual movement/waking and exclusion must be separately recorded controller outcomes; prose never fabricates an escort or waking. Do not silently give Lee this sleep effect; his approved defensive policy remains distinct until separately reconciled.

## 4. Daily rhythm and interruptions — owner-confirmed baseline, implementation proposal

Owner confirms roughly Lee’s routine, with storage stability, organization and detail/record accuracy as her priorities. Existing real coverage/handovers are reused; this does not author new shopping, sleep, meals or offsite activities. Primary overlap with Lee’s09–17 management: storage-location reconciliation, form-condition/stability review from actual implemented records, customer questions and handover. Outside that block, available co-manager/on-call support when actually present, with quiet organization or hands-on puzzles when service permits. Musical taste is a preference, not an authored listening routine. No unapproved exact endless shift rotation or per-minute busywork.

Priorities: real urgent storage/security incident → already accepted customer service/coverage → agreed current conversation → ordinary records review → optional personal activity. Lee handles actual security escalation where available. She finishes an atomic transfer safely before conversational interruption, preserves incomplete work and explains the pause. Real callers, correct rooms, route time and coverage are required; no teleporting, simultaneous counter and storage work, fabricated incident or unrecorded all-day output. Optional short breaks require actual handover; exact routine windows can be tuned during facility design.

## Required human creation

All applicable descriptive parts require an explicit selection, a valid custom description, or Not specified. Human structures/counts/materials are fixed and validated independently of disabled HTML options. New players have two human feet, five toes per foot, two human legs/arms/hands/eyes/ears, five digits per hand, no tail, human nails and skin or the appropriate human eye/hair/nail tissue. Nonhuman structures and materials remain in the universal catalogue but are disabled during creation. Skin colours are Pale, Light, Tanned and Dark. General skin colour fills/inherits regional colours until a deliberate regional choice overrides it.

Custom text stays descriptive; it grants no ability, body structure or extra limb. Delimiters in custom text are normalized so it cannot inject a second canonical body-property line. Salivation and other baseline descriptive traits do not create fluids or symptoms. Only the already-approved perspiration tendency changes sweat gain.

## Approved measurement calibration

These are deterministic game-design values, not anatomical predictions or a real-world bra-sizing standard. Height reference66in, weight140lb, waist30in, hips38in, under-chest32in, shoulder width15in, shoulder-to-wrist22in, inseam30.5in. Length factor is height/66. Girth factor is sqrt((weight/140)/(height/66)). Short/Narrow0.95, Average/Medium1.00, Long/Wide/Broad1.05. Other descriptive categories do not silently acquire invented numerical definitions.

# Daniel Mercer — Sales Team Leader

Status: approved character contract; baseline implemented in v1.0.95. See [implementation, scope and tests](DANIEL-IMPLEMENTATION.md). Historical design decisions and remaining proposals follow. ## Owner-confirmed details

- Daniel is **38**, **5′11″**, with an **average build and a softer middle**. He has **brown hair kept in a professional short style**, **brown eyes**, and a **neatly trimmed, close-cropped beard**. He has no gray at his temples. This replaces the earlier broad-shouldered and unspecified dark-hair proposals.
- He leads the thirteen sales employees. Richard remains department manager, and Erin remains Richard's secretary.
- If he is present and overhears Richard giving Erin more work than fits her day, he tries to stand up for her in a joking, indirect way.
- He does not directly confront Richard. He supports Erin where he can while remaining responsible for his sales team's productivity.
- His work includes generating sales reports; networking and coordinating with Richard for sales pitches; keeping current on Technology Center products; tracking each sales employee's actual sales; and providing the sales team with monthly company safety briefings.

- Daniel and Erin are good coworkers and workplace friends. They work closely together and are both expected at all conference-room meetings. They sometimes talk over lunch.
- Daniel finds Erin attractive, is complimentary and is not overt about his feelings. Her reciprocal feelings have not been specified.

- Owner-confirmed management approach: when an employee’s sales fall behind, Daniel starts casually and becomes firmer if the problem continues.

- Daniel has been married for five years to **Crystal Mercer**. Crystal works as a **roulette table attendant at the Silver Shackle Casino** and is **not indentured**.

- Daniel and Crystal have a loving, supportive marriage and enjoy each other’s company. He worries about flirtatious customers at Crystal’s job.
- They live in **Applewood Apartments 4C: fourth floor, apartment C**. Technology Center employees outside upper management live in Applewood Apartments; the other unassigned apartment numbers remain open.

- His confirmed personal interests are quiet evenings and outings with Crystal, cooking, hiking/other outdoor activities, and enjoying and collecting wine. Some of Erin’s favorite wines came from his recommendations.

- Owner-confirmed attribute direction: **Mental specialist, with secondary strengths in Physical**. Derive the primary from the shared engine rather than hard-coding it.

## How he supports Erin

His response depends on being present and hearing enough of the exchange to understand it. He does not know about a private conversation, unseen assignment or Erin's internal thoughts. Sharing a building or receiving a generic schedule update is not enough.

His first intervention gives Richard a face-saving opportunity to ease the workload. He makes a light comment about the amount of work or the available time rather than openly challenging Richard's authority. His concern is sincere, but the delivery remains socially cautious.

Proposed voice example: "Careful, Richard. At this rate we'll need to put Erin down as an entire department."

The line is a voice reference, not an owner-authored catchphrase or an instruction to repeat it for every request. Vary it with the actual situation. Daniel must not claim to have heard a request unless the game's event record and his presence support that knowledge.

If Richard brushes the joke aside, Daniel does not escalate into a direct argument or guarantee that the task will be withdrawn. He may later check on Erin, defer his own nonurgent request, clarify a sales deadline or help with an appropriate piece of work when he actually has capacity. Those are proposed ways to express the owner's "support where he can" direction; they do not silently cancel Richard's assignment or volunteer another employee's time.

He has real limits: sales commitments, a meeting, an unfinished report or staff who need direction may prevent immediate help. Support should remain consistent with those obligations. His reluctance to confront Richard can itself become an interesting tension in his relationship with Erin, without turning him into an automatic rescuer or a hostile bystander.

## Workplace friendship and understated attraction

Owner-confirmed: Daniel and Erin are good coworkers who have to work together closely and are present at all conference-room meetings. Their friendship is a workplace friendship, including occasional conversations over lunch. Do not turn that into an established history of private dinners, dates or regular one-to-one outings away from work.

Conference-room scheduling should include both Daniel and Erin at every such meeting, as the owner specified. A scheduled meeting is still distinct from actual attendance: both actors must physically arrive through legal room routes. If an actor is prevented from attending, the save records the absence or delayed start rather than claiming a shared experience that did not occur. Do not silently reduce the attendance requirement to sales-only meetings.

Lunch conversation is occasional and depends on overlapping availability and actual presence. They can discuss the meeting they both attended, a busy morning, the team's work or ordinary personal interests already established in their profiles. They do not automatically know each other's private thoughts or unshared home events.

Daniel finds Erin attractive. He is complimentary but keeps his feelings understated. His outward behavior can convey warmth and attention without an overt declaration. Erin does not automatically know the full extent of his attraction, and his attraction does not establish her reciprocation or a romantic relationship.

Proposed voice examples:

- Appearance: "That color really suits you, Erin."
- Competence: "You kept that meeting moving. I don't think Richard noticed how much you rescued his agenda."
- Lunch: "Mind if I join you? I could use a conversation that isn't about this month's figures."

These illustrate the confirmed direction rather than adding owner-approved dialogue or a fixed compliment frequency. An appearance compliment should fit her actual visible appearance. His concern about Richard overloading Erin remains the indirect, joking support already specified; attraction does not replace his work duties or make every supportive remark an attempt to pursue her.

## Core work responsibilities

| Responsibility | Character behavior | Implementation requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Team productivity | Knows who is working on what, notices blockers and follows up on deadlines | Read actual staff assignments and availability; no random claims of completed work |
| Sales reports | Compiles and checks the team's results, explains shortfalls and highlights useful progress | Reports derive from recorded sales and completed activities; drafting, reviewing and delivering are separate states |
| Sales pitches with Richard | Exchanges ideas, discusses prospects and coordinates preparation with his manager | A shared pitch has an actual record, participants and preparation status; conversation alone grants no customer agreement or revenue |
| Product knowledge | Keeps up to speed on Technology Center products so his team can describe them accurately | Use an authored product catalog and recorded updates; do not invent product capabilities in AI prose |
| Individual sales tracking | Tracks each of the thirteen sales employees' actual sales rather than treating everyone as interchangeable | Sales records identify employee, transaction, amount and status; pending, canceled or duplicated entries do not become completed sales |
| Monthly company safety briefings | Provides a company safety briefing for his sales team every game month | One saved briefing record per defined game-month period, with real preparation, scheduled attendance and completion; no repeated briefing on reload |

His normal reporting and briefing duties are part of his leadership role. They do not generate Erin's extra-task bonus merely because she helps coordinate them. Any extra paid assignment must use its own existing authorized task/reward rules.

## Handling employees whose sales fall behind

Owner-selected direction: **starts casually, becoming firmer if the problem continues**. His friendly everyday manner and responsibility for results are both present; his first response is not automatically a formal warning.

The following stages and dialogue are proposed expressions of that confirmed direction, not new owner-approved disciplinary rules:

| Situation | Approach | Example voice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First observed shortfall | A casual check-in about how things are going and what is getting in the way | "How are those accounts treating you? Anything getting stuck?" |
| Shortfall continues after an earlier conversation | More specific follow-up using actual results and the previously discussed issue | "We talked about those follow-ups. Walk me through what happened since then." |
| Repeated unresolved problem | A firm conversation about what needs to improve and a concrete follow-up point | "I need a clear plan for getting this back on track. What can you deliver, and by when?" |
| Recorded improvement | Acknowledge the progress and adjust the follow-up to the current situation | "Those follow-ups are moving again. Good work—keep me posted on the two still outstanding." |

He remembers who he spoke to, what concern was raised, any agreed next step and the later results. One poor outcome or failed roll does not invent a history of underperformance. Repeated button clicks or reloads do not advance the conversation from casual to firm. A remembered concern must be updated when results change rather than trap the employee in permanent escalation.

Use employee-specific sales records and actual work opportunities. A lack of assigned accounts, an approved absence or a known product/document blocker cannot be silently narrated as laziness. The precise sales targets, review period and any disciplinary consequences remain open design decisions. This personality choice does not automatically authorize firing, fines, pay deductions or a confrontation with Richard.

When implemented, use shared Mental-primary actions, ordinary legal physical actions/reactions and the existing action budgets, costs and defenses. Do not unlock a second full specialist move set merely because the Physical alignment score is second highest. Proposed encounter tendencies: assess the opponent and use legal Mental pressure/control while resources permit; use physical defense or a counter when the current engine allows it; respond to depleted resources and defeat using ordinary civilian rules. Exact tactical policy, resource tuning and aggression consequences still need implementation and tests.

## Proposed work rhythm

These timings are authoring proposals, not new owner-approved schedule values. His confirmed responsibilities should shape the actual schedule rather than appear only in a biography.

- Early workday: review individual sales and current commitments; identify a practical blocker or priority for the team.
- Morning: follow up with staff and check the latest approved product information or pitch material.
- Midday: a real lunch/break window around the team's staggered availability.
- Afternoon: work on sales reports, pitch preparation or an arranged exchange with Richard; continue checking material sales changes.
- End of workday: leave a usable handover and record the next unresolved priority.
- Monthly: prepare and deliver the sales team's company safety briefing in an available room at a recorded time.

A pitch meeting, urgent account issue or monthly briefing can displace a normal block. Already completed steps stay complete; he does not restart a report simply because the minute tick runs again. Movement between his sales workstation, Richard's office, conference room and break room uses the existing legal doors and travel costs.

# Universal directed relationships — current owner rule

One signed **−100…+100 relationship value** belongs to one stable entity and one stable player. Applies to existing/future NPCs, conscious forms, other forms and encountered entities. A bar does not create consciousness in an inanimate object. Trust is an interpretation of relationship, not a second social meter. Influence, stress, mastery, ownership, permission and consent remain distinct.

## Owner-defined meanings

| Score reached | NPC interpretation | Conscious form interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| +25 | Favorable familiarity/recognition | Familiarity and appreciation |
| −25 | Unfavorable familiarity/recognition | Negative familiarity; response is character-specific |
| +50 | Trusted; less inclined to watch closely | More trusting |
| −50 | Heavily distrusted; watched more carefully | Distrust; no automatic control penalty |
| +75 | Friend | Friend; more receptive to reasonable requests consistent with schedule/commitments |
| −75 | Enemy/adversarial; unwelcome where a particular establishment's policy applies | Adversarial; no automatic takeover |
| +100 | Close friend, almost family; warmly welcomed | Close confidant and mutual respect for shared lived experience |
| −100 | May become hostile | Deeply negative relationship; exact reaction remains authored |

Intermediate values retain the strongest reached band. These are attitudes, not automatic combat, access, stealth success, romance, disclosure or mastery grants. Forms' negative interpretations beyond the owner's explicit positive examples are conservative descriptive defaults. Legitimate resistance/release, ordinary refusals and setting boundaries do not receive an invented relationship penalty.

A known person can be neutrally familiar below 25; the threshold establishes favorable/unfavorable association. A relationship does not reveal a hidden player's original identity through an unfamiliar appearance. Keep actual recognition evidence, public identity and relationship separate.

## Shared implementation

`relationships.js` supplies typed IDs, per-player records, aliases/migration, signed clamping, event deduplication, encounter discovery, tier meanings and reaction-policy registration. Example keys are `npc:priya`, `form:kibbles`, `entity:<stable-instance-id>`. Explicit NPC/form/entity IDs with the same suffix are separate. A small whitelist maps genuine legacy aliases to their existing entity, including historical Erin labels; it does not merge arbitrary matching names or types.

Records live under `world.relationships.actors[entityId][playerId]`. JSON save/reload preserves values, event receipts and per-pair memory. New local characters receive a persisted unique local identity unless an explicit player ID already exists; existing legacy identities remain compatible. Stable player identity survives changing forms and moving the character save to another slot. A different player's record starts independently. Schema-1 records migrate without summing scores or resetting canon. Canonical records win ambiguous alias collisions; the other record is archived in `migrationConflicts`. Old actor and Dev scalar snapshots cannot copy another player's relationship into a fresh pair. Existing canonical scores also take precedence over stale unbound Dev snapshots.

Native NPC fields bind to this same store. Kibbles and arbitrary owned forms bind through the shared form path. Erin's historical `trust` property is a compatibility alias to her relationship; it is not independently stored/adjustable social progress. Historical divergent values are retained in legacy provenance while existing canonical relationship wins. Existing mastery flags/progress are not revoked. Her established cooperative route now reads relationship 100, with its existing controller conditions; no generic all-form mastery reward is added.

Care no longer awards both a social point and a separate trust point. Erin's daily considerate-care allowance and remembered topics are per player. Canine care/boundary/promise memories and social event receipts are scoped to the relevant pair; unrelated environmental events remain physical-world records. Conversation history is partitioned by player AND actor, with a current-player compatibility view for existing consumers. A new player never receives the other player's private AI conversation.

`relationship-ui.js` adds bars to the ordinary Stats drawer for encountered NPCs, owned/encountered forms and encountered entities. It reads canonical pair values, not the active form's score as a fallback for another target. Named entity identities remain stable; anonymous combat instances receive persisted distinct IDs so two same-named opponents do not share one meter. This remains a local-save game; no authenticated multiplayer transport is implemented by these changes.

## Reactions and future content

Every new entity definition must provide positive triggers, negative triggers, actual deltas, preconditions, event identity/cooldown, recipient and fallback/AI portrayal. Existing known characters have distinct policy descriptions. Actual controllers apply changes through `event`/`social`; generated prose never changes scores. # Epi-Center — Player Attribute System (Owner Proposal, 2026-10-26)

**Status:** Owner-proposed foundational mechanics; **not implemented or accepted as gameplay**. Priority moved ahead of UI reference drawers after v0.8.82 visibly displayed new toolbar. Do not modify accepted save key, original profile, or active form mechanics until migration and tests are designed.

## Five domains; ten attributes

| Domain | Internal (Defensive) | External (Offensive) |
|---|---|---|
| Body | Endurance | Fitness |
| Senses | Intuition | Reflexes |
| Mind | Focus / Willpower | Reasoning |
| Spirit | Stability | Presence |
| Social | Empathy / Insight | Influence / Intimidation |

**Internal** governs endurance, recovery, processing and resisting pressure. **External** governs speed, impact, expression and influencing outcomes. Labels are functional emphases, not absolute prohibitions on use in other checks.

## Allocation and modifier proposal

- Owner specifies **85 allocation points at character creation**, **155 maximum points**, **70 additional points found/earned**, and **maximum 16 allocated points to an attribute during creation**. **OWNER CONFIRMED 2026-10-26:** All ten attributes begin at **0** during character creation. Exactly **85 points** are distributed directly as attribute scores across all ten. The 155 total maximum is 85 creation points plus 70 additional points earned or discovered in gameplay. Creation cap is 16 per attribute. Do not grant any automatic baseline points. **Still open:** whether final 0 is allowed, and what 0 means mechanically; score 1 is listed as failure.
- Score/modifier landmarks: **1 = fail**, **2 = −4**, **4 = −3**, **6 = −2**, **8 = −1**, **10 = baseline +0**, **12 = +1**, **14 = +2**, **16 = +3**, **18 = +4**, **20 = succeed**. **Open question:** how odd scores are treated; provisional interpretation is each even threshold covers following odd score (2–3, 4–5, etc), except 1 and 20; also clarify whether 1/20 are automatic results or modifiers.
- Owner specifies **Stability 20 raises normal form influence thresholds for speech/actions by 10** (wording: “Normal percentiles for form influence over speech and actions are raised 20 in this stat raises by ten”). Clarify exact scaling and threshold behavior before implementing.

## Per-attribute mechanics

- **Endurance (Body / Internal):** reduces combat fatigue accumulation; increases out-of-combat health recovery. Example: prolonged fights and injury recovery.
- **Fitness (Body / External):** strength checks, grappling, forcing doors; physical transformation resistance rolls.
- **Intuition (Senses / Internal):** surprise-attack detection, hidden items, subtle environmental cues, lies.
- **Reflexes (Senses / External):** dodge checks, turn priority (higher first unless surprised).
- **Focus / Willpower (Mind / Internal):** reduces form influence gain; reduces roll penalties from hunger/bladder and other pressures.
- **Reasoning (Mind / External):** buying/selling/barter prices; logical arguments to bypass high-influence restrictions.
- **Stability (Spirit / Internal):** autonomy persistence and resistance to form control; influence threshold adjustments as above.
- **Presence (Spirit / External):** performance, charisma-like aura, physical grace, attracting attention.
- **Empathy / Insight (Social / Internal):** relationship accrual; additional knowledge from surroundings / reference Guide completion; NPC motives and emotional pressure.
- **Influence / Intimidation (Social / External):** persuasion, intimidation, negotiation, verbal dialogue bonuses.

## Resource and survival meters

**Health:** base character 100, adjusted by form and rarity. **Stamina:** base character 100, adjusted by form and rarity; limits combat actions and is affected by Hunger/Fatigue.

**Hunger:** 0–100; +4/hour since last meal; eating resets to 0. Hourly degradation based on hunger band:

| Hunger | Stamina degradation/hour | Health degradation/hour |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0–25 | 0 | 0 |
| 26–50 | +1 | 0 |
| 51–75 | +2 | 0 |
| 76–99 | +3 | 0 |
| 100 | +3 | +1 |

**Bladder:** 0–100; +4/hour since restroom; restroom resets to 0. Focus/Willpower roll penalty: 0–25 = 0; 26–50 = −1; 51–75 = −2; 76–100 = −3. No stamina loss was specified for bladder.

**Fatigue:** 0–100; +4/hour since full sleep; full rest resets to 0. Hourly degradation:

| Fatigue | Stamina degradation/hour | Health degradation/hour |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0–25 | 0 | 0 |
| 26–50 | +1 | 0 |
| 51–75 | +2 | 0 |
| 76–99 | +3 | 0 |
| 100 | +3 | +1 |

**Interpretation requiring confirmation:** “+1/+2/+3 stamina degradation/hour” means stamina **lost** per elapsed hour, not a positive regeneration. Clarify stacking between Hunger and Fatigue, offline elapsed-time accrual, full-rest/meal durations, current forms' modifications, and whether Focus reduces the listed bladder penalties or their effects.

1. Resolve creation score floors, 85/155/70 accounting, odd score modifier treatment and 1/20 automatic outcomes.
2. Audit existing character creation, attributes, form influence, Erin autonomy, stamina/health, and time system. Design migration preserving all existing profiles and saved data; no blind reset.
3. Introduce a central attribute schema and roll resolver with unit tests; preserve existing mechanics until explicit replacement.

## Proposed character direction

Her defining contrast is competence at organizing everyone else’s day versus difficulty defending time for herself. She enjoys being useful but wants consideration rather than endless praise for enduring more work. At home she is warmer, lightly self-deprecating and capable of a dry observation. She can be hesitant without being helpless, and firm without abruptly changing personality.

Longer arc: learn to ask Richard which priority should move when a new task arrives; accept support without surrendering competence; protect an occasional evening with friends. Progress follows actual remembered choices and relationships, not a daily automatic personality upgrade. No scripted submission, romance or new punishment system is implied.

Voice examples: “I can do that. Which of the other two should wait?” At home: “Tea first. Then I might have an opinion about the rest of the evening.” With Priya: “I brought something sweet. That counts as planning ahead.” These illustrate tone, not repeatable keyword replies.

## Proposed daily rhythm

Keep established weekday wake around 07:00, weekend 08:00, work 09:00–17:00 and bedtime around 22:00. Existing route and preparation costs govern feasibility; if a full morning would make her late, shorten optional makeup/laundry/leisure rather than teleport or silently change work hours. Packing lunch should be visible alongside breakfast, with a clear office reminder when none was packed.

Morning: actual bathroom care and appropriate clothing, simple stocked breakfast, lunch preparation when possible, planner and commute. Work: greet present colleagues, prioritize accepted tasks on the computer checklist, real meetings and outputs, lunch from her own packed meal or an explicitly chosen available alternative. End work by handing in actual completed material and checking tomorrow’s commitments.

After work: return physically, change, wash/remove makeup as wanted, deal with real laundry/dishes, cook or use an existing portion. Most evenings are reading and quiet television; propose one flexible friend evening and an occasional wine discussion rather than obligations every night. Weekend: slower breakfast, household reset, groceries if actually available, book discussion or an accepted visit, then protected rest.

Priority: urgent needs and hard commitments first; existing authority/mastery decides who chooses. A live conversation or accepted visit pauses optional chores with a natural warning before departure. In mastered/zero-influence states these are suggestions or explicitly delegated routines, never forced takeover. Missed optional leisure creates no punishment. Inactive Erin advances none of this offscreen.

## Owner-confirmed voluntary delegation after mastery

Mastery preserves permanent achievement and player authority; it must not permanently silence the form or prohibit consensual autonomous activity. A player can discuss and explicitly delegate control to an active conscious form for a particular routine, a chosen interval, or the remainder of the day through an agreed bedtime endpoint. Examples: “Take charge for your night routine,” “Take over for an hour,” or “You can lead today until bedtime.” The form can express willingness, practical constraints and alternatives. Discussion alone is not authorization; resolve a clear affirmative agreement using canonical action handling.

Delegation is a separately saved, revocable agreement, not loss of mastery, renewed influence, a new resistance contest or mandatory trust cost. The player can reclaim control at any time without a saving throw or penalty. Stop further autonomous decisions immediately; represent safe interruption of a physical action honestly rather than instantly completing it or undoing already consumed supplies. Show who is currently leading, agreed scope/end and a readily available Take charge again action. Clarify ambiguous endpoints; a bedtime routine should complete only within the agreed scope, and delegation must not silently extend through overnight sleep or into the next day.

Use the form’s authored capabilities, existing schedule and available real resources. Existing single-routine delegation may be reused, but broader duration/day agreements are not assumed already implemented. Agreement survives reload with the same canonical game-time endpoint and no offline simulation. Expiry, explicit revocation, release, body change, death/incapacitation or invalid state ends/suspends delegation safely as appropriate; it cannot transfer authority to a different form or create a duplicate offscreen person. No invented travel, unlimited spending, social/intimate consent or circumvention of curse/combat/capability gates follows from routine delegation. Additional commitments or exceptional decisions remain explicit choices under their own rules.

Universal applicability: conscious forms with an authored decision/schedule adapter can support this contract. Inanimate flats do not acquire an independent shoe personality or movement, and delegating to a cat form does not control Priya. Owner-approved rule; exact interval presets, willingness presentation and implementation state remain to be designed/tested. Acceptance: mastered routine delegation, interval/day expiry, mid-task reclaim, reload, real supply/time accounting, no mastery/influence changes, form switches/release and clear frontend/AI control context.

Hands, forehead and neck are the exposed-region request baseline. ## Earned one-item vouchers

First record-breaking completion per player per cabinet grants one saved single-use five-percent voucher: at most three. Subsequent plays may improve the leaderboard but cannot farm more vouchers. One voucher adds **five percentage points** to the valid purchase discount:0→5,10→15,15→20. This is additive percentage-point stacking, not a sequential five-percent reduction. Only one voucher applies to one positively priced purchased item, never a service, free storage action or entire basket. Manager selection and shared-negative suspension of manager courtesy remain intact; the arcade reward is separately earned. Whole-gold prices still round upward. If rounding would produce no additional saving, reject applying the voucher and retain it. Vouchers have no expiry.

Quote previews never consume a voucher. The future checkout hook requires a matching player, item, current quote and resolved purchase receipt, validates attendant/rate/eligibility again, and consumes once. Cancelled, stale or invalid transactions cannot consume it. Receipt replay is idempotent. **There is no actual item stock or player checkout yet.** The hook is tested with explicit synthetic receipts and does not create a sale, supply an item or charge gold. # Universal form resistance drawer — owner-approved UI rule

All worn forms use the same collapsible Internal resistance drawer. It stays blue while no actual roll is eligible and turns green when the actual native controller offers resistance. This is one rule across living, animal, humanoid and inanimate forms. It does not add a new source of rolls or grant an action to a display-only/unbuilt form.

The highlight is optional-action information. It never rolls, spends resources, changes influence/mastery, starts movement, forces a decision, opens the drawer or creates a new popup. The player chooses a button or equivalent typed action. Voluntarily approaching a pack or pursuing prey is the player's choice, not an automatic resistance request. An actual form-origin urge may offer resistance; the player's selected travel/action does not manufacture that opportunity or count as a missed check.

## Shared implementation

`resistance-availability.js` provides the read-only `assess` projection. Its inputs are actual native form timing, Resolve, full/prerequisite state, mastery/binding/combat gates and independently eligible decision/escape opportunities. Standard influence resistance/desperate/recovery honors the saved internal-action cooldown; paid resistance is disabled below three Resolve while zero-cost desperate resistance remains an opportunity above zero Resolve. Rendering does not initialize a clock, call RNG or mutate game state.

The drawer's `data-ready` value drives the global blue/green CSS. Actual action buttons remain attached to their existing native controller; a stale menu or text request still encounters the controller's authoritative guards. New adapters must supply real eligibility and route actions through that controller rather than implement a second die/cost/mode or set a cosmetic green state.

`formMindMarkup` keeps Erin and Kibbles, dispatches the actual cat and object-form panels, and leaves unsupported native forms blue with an explicit missing-controller reason. Preeti and Pri use `catResistanceMarkup` with their existing `EpiPriyaCat.internal` actions. Priya's flats use the same readiness contract and their existing recovery controller, retaining actual first-wear prerequisites. Cat/flats resistance buttons now sit in this common drawer; their body/location controls stay in the nearby panel.

Navigation inserts exactly one common drawer across normal and special room layouts. Combat enters the blocked common dock before building guarded household controls; this fixes a render failure when an actual cat encounter is active inside Priya's apartment. Collapsed/open state and the normal front-dock behavior remain controlled by player choices and the existing interaction-state mechanism.

## Readiness scope

- An ordinary cooldown becoming due can highlight the drawer.
- A separately eligible current-decision or escape roll can highlight it while influence resistance is cooling down.
- Mastery, permanent binding, active combat or missing physical prerequisites suppress the internal rolls where the existing native controller prohibits them.
- Continuing encasement is not itself a resistance roll and no longer produces a false green highlight by itself.
- Reading/expanding a drawer cannot execute resistance.
- An unimplemented form such as Markus does not advertise a fabricated action. Its future native conquest/instinct adapter must use this common contract when an actual roll is implemented.

## Text and verification

Existing text-to-controller matching is retained. Common aliases include “resist influence,” “resist the form,” “resist this urge,” “attempt desperate resistance,” “regain composure,” and “resist this decision” where the corresponding actual control exists. Owner request: provide a non-graphic controller-resolved private encounter record, classified `explicit_adult`, including the infected NPC's active archetype, actual transmission outcome and a current-body Arousal reset when climax is recorded. ## Implemented

- `rebuild/hub/intimate-encounter.js` is loaded by the hub. Authored scene controllers call `begin` only after resolving mutual agreement, prior infection disclosure, privacy, the carrier's archetype and an actual fluid-contact route. These flags are mechanical results, not fields to accept from a model or raw player JSON. Existing carrier permission/presence gates still apply.
- The controller records a fresh source/contact in `bimbo-virus-exposure.js`. It uses the real game clock and existing route thresholds, sample lifetime, hidden Endurance checks and incubation controller. Caller-supplied timestamps cannot fabricate elapsed game time. No infection percentage or numeric acute reaction is invented.
- `complete` closes the contact and records only checks attributed to that contact. Failed resistance can begin incubation; successful resistance or sub-threshold contact cannot. Private die/DC details stay in the saved mechanical record; narrative metadata contains only the outcome. Another contact's infection is not attributed to this encounter.
- A controller-recorded climax sets only the active body's Arousal to zero. Without that recorded outcome there is no reset. Independent existing resource-floor effects remain separate. Stable player identity, unrelated body resources and previous incubation are preserved.
- Cancellation, lost co-presence, changed body and missing agreement prevent completion. Completed event IDs are idempotent through reload: no repeated reset, feed entry or roll.
- `completeIntimateEncounter` connects the result to the private feed and existing serialized worker payload with `tone: explicit_adult`. `EpiIntimateEncounter.payload` also builds the serialized scene directly. The event remains a concise fade-to-black record; the generator is instructed to summarize only recorded non-graphic facts and cannot decide consent, contact or infection.
- Archetype labels are `gym_bunny`, `sorority`, and `club_bimbo`.

# Kibbles canine consciousness — owner character specification (questions 1–20, 2026-11-02)

**Status:** Owner-provided behavioral design; design only, not gameplay implementation. “Bella” is an instance-specific name, **not the universal name**. Every player's Kibbles form may have a player-chosen name and gender; retain the established one-time choice after mastery. Do not hardcode female pronouns. The owner's wording below uses female pronouns for their instance.

## Nature and identity
- Genuine canine mind, no words; communicates via senses, impulses, emotion, mental imagery. Persistent unmastered presence; after mastery can voluntarily provide sensory insights without overriding player intent.
- Capable intelligent working dog, not human; recognizes the player is not a dog but does not understand human concepts of transformation/mastery/captivity. Feels whole rather than hollow after defeating/encasing player; regards player as overcome prey/opponent without malice.
- Archetype temperament weights: Physical = loyal/protective; Mental = curious/obedient; Arousal = playful/mischievous. One core personality, not three distinct entities.
- Primary desire: be a good dog, be fed/praised/free at lower influence, potentially accept a **kind** owner at higher influence; player helping interpret and satisfy canine impulses builds goodwill, while ignoring obvious needs despite human knowledge frustrates. Human-style commands or “bad dog” damage relationship; contextual “good girl/boy” after genuine helpful action is welcome.

## Territory, needs, social life
- Home/territory is original alley near Central Hub between Spire and outer loop; roaming dog packs usually avoid this inner area. Home crate holds favorite ball and worn blanket; unauthorized touching/removal prompts warning/aggression.
- Immediately after encasement food-seeking is strong. Can eat garbage, has canine digestive tract. Accepting food is not instant trust; may initially avoid taking from a hand. Hunger >=70% makes food a priority **if no food is stored in crate**.
- With other dogs: cautious until reading scent markers/personality/gender; with strangers: sniff/investigate, reject rushed collaring/ownership, respect autonomy earns trust; familiar humans: may help/follow but wary of rooms with doors that close; friendly/playful/protective toward children; guarded/defensive toward authority.
- Enjoys petting but limited brushing; praise for completed actions; cuddling/belly rubs/close contact only with deep familiarity and trust (cuddling additionally if collared in owner's example); wary of rushed ownership. Seeks people of the same gender as its selected instance.
- Likes fetch, chase, tug, swimming, digging, scent-tracking, exploration; chasing squirrel wandering hub periphery especially enticing.
- Knows sit, stay, roll over, beg, speak, shake; dominant persona (e.g. Elizabeth) may command a few; treat improves compliance; praise follows performed behavior; familiar trust increases willingness for vulnerable commands such as roll over.
- Fears loud noises, abrupt movements, weapons, bright flashing lights; severe distrust of confinement by unfamiliar people; medical procedures provoke aggressive fear. On encountering roaming dog pack, fights/resists; if leashed, warns handler before encounter.

## Daily schedule and priorities
- Seek food at sunrise, midday, sunset; explore park, chase squirrel when paths cross; light naps near hub periphery if unengaged; deep sleep in crate.
- Easily distracted if roaming within outer loop; attractive food, engagement or concern about territorial security can redirect chase/play. Another dog's scent in home alley interrupts sleep; protecting a trusted human outranks treat.
- Significant environmental triggers: unfamiliar territorial scent, distress, threats. Exceptional high-influence triggers: intrusion by crate, attempted capture, storm; additional events may include another canine or strong fresh food smells where justified.
- A player challenging a high-influence routine must contest or offer a genuinely more appealing canine alternative; don't treat the routine as rigid human scheduling.
- Unattended behaviors derive from routine, context, and archetype weights, not unlimited idle rolls.

## Relationship
- Gains trust from respecting boundaries, consistent care, interpreting desires, helping satisfy wants with player's knowledge.
- Loses trust from “bad dog”, careless interactions with other dogs, harsh/demanding treatment, and especially broken promises (e.g. promising food then tricking it into seeking help from a friend).
- Trust and influence are distinct. Accepting a scrap does not imply accepting collar, owner, command, or captivity. Positive reinforcement must be event-specific, not text-spammable.

## Universal rules to preserve
- Influence control bands, autonomous event cadence and conditional exceptional third attempt, 30-in-game-minute internal action eligibility, original Willpower vs form Reasoning, 3 Resolve / 0 Resolve -2 / +6 recovery, successful resistance -10 influence/+10 progress, failure +5 influence, completed forced activity +5 influence, and rarity-specific mastery/escape rules remain in COMBAT-FOUNDATIONS-GUIDE.md.
- Kibbles has no zipper/seam; mastered Kibbles release is by will, with no free healing. Existing snack route is an independently authored mastery route. No automatic body changes reversal or assumed gender before player choice.
- Do not conflate dog instincts with human-level verbal reasoning, or penalize legitimate resistance as abuse.

## Owner answers 21–30 (2026-11-02)

21. **Forgiveness:** Easy to earn, particularly for encased player. Other characters can soothe with treats or gentle words except serious violations such as rushed collaring/kenneling.
22. **Voluntary shared control:** Kibbles can yield some control even at high influence but may become distracted and forget permission mid-activity. It will not willingly pass the **outer loop road** boundary. Preserve player challenge/contest rules.
23. **Cooperative release, not easy mastery:** No generic trust-based mastery for Kibbles. Bored Kibbles may consider releasing encased player if they promise appealing play, belly rubs or similar attention. Very strong relationship **plus actual follow-through** might warrant further special consideration, but do not invent a mastery threshold or automatic mastery. Voluntary release is distinct from base mastery.
24. **Relationship declines:** Repeated complaining, calling it a bad dog, denying appealing snacks/treats, or repeatedly resisting to pursue boring actions frustrate Kibbles. No unapproved numeric penalties.
25. **Onset:** Distinct canine mental presence starts **once player's head is fully encased**, regardless of total transformation percent.
26. **Influence-driven sensory prompts:** Higher influence intensifies attention to new/appealing scents, rapid movement, loud sounds/ear flicks, toys, offered ball throws, salivation at treats, and words linked to pleasant outcomes (walk/play/treat). Lower influence reduces intrusive prompts/automatic responses, not canine existence.
27. **Embodied perspective:** High kinetic energy, taut action-ready muscles, rapidly shifting emotion, impatience/boredom in inactivity; mental imagery focuses on movement, ball, attention. Activity is exhilarating; prolonged isolation dull and interminable, reflecting dependence on others for engagement.
28. **Collar/leash/kennel and handler:** With **trusted other player**, collar represents consistency/partnership; leash represents walk and loyalty to holder; kennel frustrates freedom, proximity and ability to protect handler. These shift focus to handler and **make internal resistance harder** without automatically reducing form-player relationship. Do not invent numeric modifiers yet. Untrusted forced collar/kennel remains a boundary violation.
29. **Reduced pressure:** Bored after no interaction, or absorbed in pleasant mindless eating/chewing bone; strongest opportunities when not collared, leashed or kenneled. Distinguish sensory desire from pressure and resistance opportunities.
30. **Physical escape:** Successful eligible 1d50 escape check results in Kibbles' throat/mouth distending to **hack/regurgitate the player out**. No zipper/seam, no ordinary peeling; escaping is not mastery. Eligibility, anatomy and release effects require authored implementation.

40. **Long-term:** Player usually will not remain unmastered long enough for substantial character development, but intentional prolonged experience can alter learned behaviors. Excitable energy and archetype-specific two core traits are permanent.

# Kibbles combat and AI — owner decisions

Status: implemented in the v1.0.41 enemy AI candidate; automated validation passed, owner manual acceptance pending. This does not complete wearable restoration or post-defeat continuation. ## Confirmed

- Ultimate goal: encase the player. Health defeat and direct encasement are both acceptable approaches; use attack variety rather than defaulting repeatedly to Skin Wrap.
- Bite: Main action, 8 Stamina, 12 Health damage on a successful hit; uses 1d20 + Fitness against applicable physical defense. Health damage only: no restraint, attachment or transformation progress.
- Grapple: establishes contact/restraint, not transformation. Skin Wrap is a separate move. Early contact priorities are head/neck and hands; existing source also allows multiple legally earned contact fronts and behavior-sensitive switches. Do not invent a new random-only targeting policy.
- Any head encasement above 0% occupies Kibbles' head and disables Bite immediately, not only at full coverage. An unavailable Bite must never be selected as fallback.
- While no attachment/restraint has been established, approved basic mix is Bite/Grapple 50/50, subject to the newly requested pre-wrap Pouncing Bite opening phase and resource eligibility.
- While restrained or still tethered by any encased body portion, eligible Bite/Skin Wrap mix is 50/50 when the head is not occupied. Existing body attachment permits connected-region Skin Wrap even after restraint is escaped; re-Grapple is not required merely because restraint ended.
- With head coverage and an existing tether, use Skin Wrap when affordable; recover when no legal affordable attack is available. If there is no remaining attachment or restraint, establish legal contact again before wrapping.
- Escape Physical Restraint and active resistance to physical transformation/peeling attachment are separate. Breaking Grapple does not automatically remove encasement. A peeling action requires actual usable anatomy; no hands/zipper shortcut through a fully sealed form.
- If Kibbles is restrained, prioritize Wriggle Free as a Minor. On the first failed attempt, use the Main to recover Stamina. After the second successive failed attempt, attempt legal Bite with the Main that same turn. After a fallback Bite, make a hidden decision roll selecting one or two escape attempts for the next cycle; do not reset to a fixed two every time. If head coverage makes Bite unavailable, prioritize Skin Wrap over Wriggle Free when attachment allows wrapping. Exact optional-Minor scheduling in that special case remains to be finalized without compromising the chosen Main.
- Maintain a 32 Stamina lower floor; enter recovery before ordinary attack spending would break that floor and recover until at least 60 Stamina, using legal +12 STA recovery actions. Reserve the chosen Main cost before optional Minor spending. If two successful Skin Wraps would finish encasement, Kibbles may ignore the 32-point floor for that capture opportunity, while still needing the actual action cost. Determine proximity using current legal anatomical advancement, not a fabricated free wrap or guaranteed success.
- Analyze is once per encounter. Do not re-enable it merely because a player changes form or reveals a move. Natural canine senses remain passive.
- Pouncing Bite: 12 Stamina, 20 Health damage, no attachment/transformation effect. Hidden random decision selects two or three opening attempts (hit or miss) before entering the Grapple/Skin Wrap strategy. A player Grapple attempt automatically reduces that opening limit to two; an attempt counts even if it fails. Pounce is unavailable during the attachment/wrap sequence. Once every attachment is removed and Kibbles is physically free to move, Pouncing Bite becomes available again. Do not allow a pounce merely because restraint ended while body attachment remains.

## Approved mechanics implemented

Normal resistance costs 3 Resolve; desperate costs zero with −2; recovery restores 6 capped at the existing pool maximum. Original Willpower contests form Reasoning. Success reduces influence 10 and adds 10 permanent progress; failure adds 5 influence and retains progress. These actions do not advance time. Zero influence prohibits forced override/regain.

Influence 1–24 supplies urges; 25–49 permits up to one conflicting-action contest per interval; 50–74 adds one independent attempt; 75–100 permits two independent attempts and one additional unique actual exceptional event. Genuine event IDs survive reload; no repeated idle roll loop. Quiet/absorbed windows can suppress extra pressure. Handler focus removes that quiet suppression without inventing a numeric roll modifier. Shared control can be willingly offered during a quiet window and lost to a genuine new distraction; it is not mastery. A genuinely appealing play alternative may redirect a nonurgent routine without a contest.

Common/Uncommon mastery is automatic at progress 100/influence zero. Rare/Epic use original Willpower vs authored Reasoning with form +2/+4, restoring influence 40/50 on failure and retaining progress. Legendary trials remain authored, never auto-granted. Erin's existing meaningful home-topic trust accumulation can independently reach +100 cooperative mastery. No new generic Kibbles trust-mastery threshold exists. Mastery never heals, grants tier XP or reverses established physical changes.

Actual world-origin Kibbles internal mastery resolves Hangry Fangs; returning to Eve still requires release and a human-understandable current body. # Language/context recognition follow-up — local, unpublished

Owner examples are a starting vocabulary, not a finite command list. `action-lexicon.js` supplies 39 action families plus speech/help/database/field syntax, with 113 examples and shared guidance. `build-action-lexicon.cjs` generates ACTION-LEXICON.md from this live data. Eve's “show common action phrases” response and topic suggestions use the same source.

## Parsing contract

`language-actions.js` produces mode, intent, target, quantity/reciprocity modifiers and an optional unobservable purpose:

- **Action:** “I travel to Burke’s Sweets” can start actual pathing.
- **Desire/intention:** “I want to travel …”, “I want to buy candy”, wishes/plans/future declarations and “I'd like to …” do not execute item, purchase or movement actions.
- **Purpose:** “I travel to Burke’s Sweets because I want to buy candy” starts only travel. The reason is stored as purpose, not another action. The narrator is never allowed to decide that candy was bought.
- **Speech:** “I speak aloud: ‘I want to buy candy’” speaks only the supplied words. Its contents are not reparsed into a purchase. Actual speech uses local listeners and current body capabilities.
- **Private/conditional:** thoughts, imagined actions, negation and hypothetical conditions do not execute outward actions.
- **Requests:** named counterparties can respond under actual controllers. A travel capability question previews a route rather than starting one.

Context entity resolution uses only actual current participants. Full names, unique first names, and a valid remembered target can resolve; ambiguous or absent targets cannot be guessed. Purpose is not exposed to NPCs as mind-read knowledge. Unsupported quantities are rejected rather than silently taking one item.

## Controller and feed contract

`language-actions-ui.js` maps structured requests to the existing navigation, menu/controller bridge, world-object, inventory/clothing, conversation, form and Dart controllers. Travel retains the full path graph, per-step restrictions, time/resource costs and interruptions. Flats cannot move or speak by issuing commands; their visual/listening observations use the existing ground-level flats controller. Item ownership, form binding, mastery and privacy checks remain in the original controllers.

Typing “I interact with [person]” can select a physically present conversation recipient without a menu. Object interaction opens/inspects actual offered affordances rather than guessing a destructive default. “I put [worn garment] into my inventory” uses actual unequipping rules; already-carried objects are not duplicated. “I sniff Dart back” uses the existing canine greeting, barriers and actual presence.

Social descriptors are outward controller-resolved acts without fabricated player quotations. Tits’s actual praise/compliment uses the already approved +1 kind-remark event. Flirtation creates no contact permission; bare criticism does not invent an insult quotation. Other NPCs retain their existing action/reaction policies and relationship accounting.

Controller-generated live-feed results remain authoritative for success, refusals and blocked actions. Feed entries carry only an interpretation-only `requestedAction` summary; parsing does not itself certify success. NPC social replies carry a separately controller-resolved speech-act summary. The AI’s serialized scene receives this neutral context plus the actual event outcome, not a menu label substituted for an event. Private purpose is excluded. All model prose remains unable to mutate state.

## Scope still separate

Kissing now uses the shared approved library, Tits’s actual availability policy, warning/confirmation, accepted contact and rolling exposure. See KISSING-INTERACTION.md. Other NPC acceptance policies and further owner-led body-target vocabulary remain separate.
