## Twelve-category authoring checklist

Authoring standard established from Priya’s first completion package and Erin’s refinement review. This is a design checklist, not a second runtime schema. Keep the validated living profile in [FORM-LIVING-TEMPLATE.md](FORM-LIVING-TEMPLATE.md); reuse existing clocks, inventory, navigation, encounters, relationships and mastery adapters.

## Start from a broad brief

Owner supplies a general vibe, role and any fixed constraints. Author a coherent complete first pass using the sections below; offer recommendations for missing details together, rather than asking the owner to choose every object or minute. Group review around character identity, daily life, relationships and special routes. Bring back only consequential unresolved choices. Do not manufacture past owner approval.

For every section distinguish **established canon**, **proposed default**, **implemented evidence**, **owner acceptance**, and **deferred/not applicable**. A proposal may be detailed without being implemented. Record sources, stable IDs and superseding decisions. Do not turn a historical document’s old test count into current evidence.

## 1. Identity and lifecycle

Name/aliases; adult age where relevant; species/body; pronouns; appearance and approved art/provenance; occupation; stable IDs; residence/floor/unit and discovery rules; public versus private identity. Explain whether this is an independent NPC, a conscious form, an object form, or a linked NPC/form. Define what exists while unequipped, acquired, active, released and mastered. Never duplicate a person offscreen to service a schedule.

## 2. Character and voice

Three defining traits, a contrasting trait, strengths, flaws, values, ordinary worries, ambitions and boundaries. Specify speech rhythm, humor, work/private differences, changing mood and representative short dialogue. Include interests with usable conversational substance and remembered actual events. Avoid stock keyword monologues and repeated gestures. Original-player thoughts and undisclosed form history stay private.

## 3. Capabilities and physical profile

Anatomy, senses, locomotion, speech, manipulation, clothing and equipment compatibility; actual attributes, rarity and resource ownership; ordinary civilian combat or appropriate existing animal/object limitations. Explicitly state unavailable actions. Derive gameplay numbers from the current engine and label new tuning. No copied human hands/speech, resource refills or invented powers.

## 4. Daily rhythm and interruption rules

Provide a readable weekday/weekend rhythm, work/lunch/commute, sleep, personal care, meals, exercise, hobbies, errands and social availability. Use windows and priorities rather than a compulsory minute-by-minute script. Specify actual destinations, route costs, doors/floors, preparation time and legal movement.

Resolve urgent needs, work commitments, agreed appointments, ongoing player engagement, optional routines and rest in an explicit order appropriate to the character. Describe greetings, departures, delays, cancellations and resuming interrupted work. Bulk time, live time and reload must not invent completed actions. Sleep/absence blocks unavailable interactions.

## 5. Home and personal belongings

Describe the shell separately from the character’s furniture and atmosphere. Cover living area, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, clothing storage, entrance/hall storage and special spaces. Give a consistent palette, materials, lighting and personal keepsakes. Preserve real navigation and nested drawers/Back; do not clone another character’s decor.

For each usable object define action, duration, prerequisites, owner, stock/custody, saved effect, feedback and failure state. Decorative items may be decorative, but must not advertise a nonexistent use. Include laundry/dishes/used containers and product use where applicable. Receiving food must create a usable inventory serving when intended, rather than merely describing one.

## 6. Wardrobe, care and dietary preferences

A curated individual wardrobe plus presets for the character’s actual roles: work, casual, hosting, exercise and bedtime as appropriate. Define worn/clean/dirty/stored ownership, footwear constraints, private changing and missing-stock behavior. Care includes relevant hair, skin, bathing, grooming and scent with actual effects; no medical claims from ambience.

Meals, snacks and drinks need distinct preferences, real recipes/items, finite quantities, preparation, serving, consumption and cleanup. Purchases need funds, hours, travel and custody. No automatic pantry or wardrobe replacement unless expressly designed.

## 7. Relationships, visits and social agency

Map specific people, history sources, mutual attitudes, known identity, trust and unresolved tensions. Use the one directed relationship value; keep recognition, mastery and consent separate. Define introductions, invitation/acceptance, entry permission, actual travel, hosting, room access, follow/escort, departure and follow-up. Proposed friends are not spawned actors.

Friendship, respectful dating and special transformation routes need independent eligibility. Neither high trust nor a purr is blanket consent. Define optional participation, refusal, ending contact and proportionate consequences for real actions. Do not punish ordinary declined attention as misconduct.

## 8. Work and public life

Actual workstation, tools, colleagues, products, meaningful work outputs and approachable task checklist. Track acceptance, progress, retrieved materials, meetings, submission and one-time rewards. Give meetings real turn-taking among present people, with interruption/room-directed speech. Employer property, expense allowances and wages stay separate from player inventory/funds.

## 9. Special form or quest route

Trigger versus safe examination/pickup; explicit agreement where relevant; authored transformation stages; preserved original state; physical capabilities and viewpoint; internal voice/instinct; opposition stat and meter; shared mastery/cost/cooldown/dice; gear/collar behavior; repeat acquisition; permanent completion; exact reversion conditions and reverse stages; safe placement and retained objects. Specify first-time and mastered-repeat flows separately. Mark this section not applicable when no special route is authored.

## 10. Narration and AI contract

For each important event supply an AI-off result and sensory description based on actual body/activity/presence. Emit timely movement, arrival, pressure/contact change and interruption feedback instead of long unexplained silence. Separate fictional media from world events.

AI expands recorded facts and responds to the actual conversation; it cannot move actors, spend stock, grant progress, invent dialogue as completed history, disclose private thoughts or decide consent. Give it speaker, directed/local audience, real listeners, activity, relationships and bounded recent memory. Cover disabled/failing/stale AI and duplicate prevention. Clearly distinguish mock tests from real-provider prose acceptance.

## 11. Persistence and implementation plan

List canonical modules/adapters, additive fields/migration, old-save interpretation, unique item IDs, finite budgets, exactly-once effects, interrupted jobs, reload boundaries and three-slot isolation. Do not migrate unknown history into invented attendance or relationships. Identify dependencies on unimplemented venues/NPCs. Deliver coherent playable slices with explicit limits.

## 12. Completion and verification matrix

For each promised feature record design status, runtime location, automated evidence, actual browser flow and owner acceptance. Include a normal complete day, work→home, an interrupted visit, sleep/absence, time jumps, stocked/empty inventory, ownership, reloads, alternate body, mastery/repeat route and phone navigation. Add route-specific failure/reversion tests. Use meaningful tests, not assertions that merely repeat descriptions.

Release handoff must state branch, exact runtime commit, tests, public link, blockers/limits and exact next action. Update this template whenever a character exposes a reusable missing category; keep character-specific taste and tuning in that character’s dossier. “First playable package complete” does not mean all future content or personal acceptance is finished.

## Owner-confirmed conversation and departure rule

When a player is actively engaging an NPC or conscious form, a scheduled routine must not silently remove them or abruptly cut off the exchange. The character acknowledges the next activity, explains any need to leave and gives a natural conversational close before actual movement or action. Optional routines can wait; interaction may cause a real, recorded delay. Hard commitments and urgent needs still matter and should be communicated, not erased. No indefinite conversation lock, invented attendance, teleport or offscreen duplicate is implied. For an internal form, communicate the intended activity within existing authority/mastery rules rather than pretending the consciousness walks away. Exact grace periods and interruption mechanics remain implementation work, not an owner-approved fixed timer. Applies universally to future NPC/form designs.

## Owner-confirmed sustained activities and fine interactions

Player-initiated leisure/care must be a recognized current activity, not only a furniture toggle or a clock jump. Examples: watch television (distinct from turning it on/selecting a channel), read the chosen book, take a bath, lie awake on the bed, and take a chosen-duration nap (including about two hours) rather than mandatory full-night sleep. Form/NPC dialogue and bounded narration should reflect the actual ongoing activity, remaining duration and recent completion. Existing autonomous and manual versions must share activity completion/satisfaction facts.

Provide meaningful start/continue/stop or finish behavior, appropriate physical posture/location, real elapsed time and ability to interrupt; retain progress/state on reload. Watching fiction should produce authored evolving content and contextual conversation, not merely a channel label. Reading should expose current title/chapter/activity without requiring the player to navigate the shelf again for every continuation. Preserve manual chapter choice. Bath products, coverage, water/preparation and elapsed effects remain real; lying down is not sleeping, and a nap must not silently become an eight-hour sleep. Urgent needs, commitments and existing form authority govern interruptions without silently erasing the activity. Exact duration options and update cadence remain implementation tuning, not fixed by this design note. Do not award a full session’s benefits at start or after cancellation, duplicate effects on reload, or invent actions skipped by time jumps.

Erin-specific restoration request: the long couch should have its intended throw blanket, with an actual pull-over/use interaction while reading/resting and removal/put-back behavior. ## Owner-confirmed voluntary delegation after mastery

Mastery preserves permanent achievement and player authority; it must not permanently silence the form or prohibit consensual autonomous activity. A player can discuss and explicitly delegate control to an active conscious form for a particular routine, a chosen interval, or the remainder of the day through an agreed bedtime endpoint. Examples: “Take charge for your night routine,” “Take over for an hour,” or “You can lead today until bedtime.” The form can express willingness, practical constraints and alternatives. Discussion alone is not authorization; resolve a clear affirmative agreement using canonical action handling.

Delegation is a separately saved, revocable agreement, not loss of mastery, renewed influence, a new resistance contest or mandatory trust cost. The player can reclaim control at any time without a saving throw or penalty. Stop further autonomous decisions immediately; represent safe interruption of a physical action honestly rather than instantly completing it or undoing already consumed supplies. Show who is currently leading, agreed scope/end and a readily available Take charge again action. Clarify ambiguous endpoints; a bedtime routine should complete only within the agreed scope, and delegation must not silently extend through overnight sleep or into the next day.

Use the form’s authored capabilities, existing schedule and available real resources. Existing single-routine delegation may be reused, but broader duration/day agreements are not assumed already implemented. Agreement survives reload with the same canonical game-time endpoint and no offline simulation. Expiry, explicit revocation, release, body change, death/incapacitation or invalid state ends/suspends delegation safely as appropriate; it cannot transfer authority to a different form or create a duplicate offscreen person. No invented travel, unlimited spending, social/intimate consent or circumvention of curse/combat/capability gates follows from routine delegation. Additional commitments or exceptional decisions remain explicit choices under their own rules.

Universal applicability: conscious forms with an authored decision/schedule adapter can support this contract. Inanimate flats do not acquire an independent shoe personality or movement, and delegating to a cat form does not control Priya. Owner-approved rule; exact interval presets, willingness presentation and implementation state remain to be designed/tested. Acceptance: mastered routine delegation, interval/day expiry, mid-task reclaim, reload, real supply/time accounting, no mastery/influence changes, form switches/release and clear frontend/AI control context.

# Perspiration — implemented locally, unpublished

## Activity and clock

`rebuild/hub/perspiration.js` owns persisted actor/body-specific perspiration. Player travel and room movement use the canonical game clock. Walking including travel reaches10 after60 active game minutes; continued walking adds5 per15 minutes. Jogging reaches25 after30 minutes, then adds10 per10 minutes. An active controller-resolved, mutually agreed private encounter reaches25 after20 active minutes, then adds10 per10 minutes. Encounter prose alone never establishes activity. Mixed activities preserve normalized exertion progress. No offline catch-up is added; duplicate timestamps and reloads cannot advance twice.

After10 inactive minutes, body perspiration drops5 every5 game minutes. Incomplete exertion progress drops1/12 per five-minute drying step, reaching zero after60 drying minutes. Clothing moisture declines separately and soiling persists. Per-minute NPC schedulers feed Priya, Richard, Daniel, Nadia, Charity and Tits; unrecorded activities are not inferred from generated prose. The existing private-encounter adapter supplies activity only while its actual agreement, body, partner and space remain valid. No new encounter permissions or natural-language ingestion triggers are introduced.

## Body regions

The hidden global score is exertion state, not literal percentage skin coverage. Regional surfaces are armpits, under-chest fold, inner thighs, feet, hands, forehead, neck and spine. Default multipliers are1.2 for armpits,1.1 for under-chest folds/inner thighs/spine,1 for forehead/neck/feet,0.6 for hands. Without an authored under-chest fold, that region uses0.5; authored thigh friction increases its local factor by20%. These are gameplay approximations, not universal sex-based physiological claims. Player features use recorded appearance; NPC adapters support explicit anatomy flags, with Tits’s authored full chest/thigh build represented. Missing anatomy does not invent a sex or body shape.

Known enclosed footwear starts local foot moisture after30 actual worn minutes, adding0.5 per active minute or0.25 while stationary, capped100. Footwear removal reduces that retained surface moisture1 per minute. Recorded nervousness can raise hand moisture independently, capped40; no dialogue guesses at nervousness. Production timestamps remain separate from drying timestamps for future contact-source validation.

## Visibility and narrator

Numerical scores remain hidden. Below50 is not readily noticeable to others;50–74 is visibly sweaty;75–99 heavily sweaty;100 dripping sweat. Observation requires actual same-space presence. Public context projects only exposed forehead/neck/hand descriptions, never covered under-chest/thigh/foot facts, full hidden meters or remote NPC state. Inanimate flats do not gain a human visual survey or produce sweat themselves. Their private sensory records use Priya’s actual regional foot moisture, wear time and pressure. Observation/rendering does not simulate activity.

The player's status shows a qualitative body description. Typed examination of a nearby NPC includes visible sweat when applicable. Shared AI physical context carries only locally observable qualitative sweat facts. No automatic NPC comments, advice, rest requests or global broadcasts were added.

## Clothing and footwear

Actually recorded worn garments gain moisture only on their covered regions. Direct garments gain up to1 moisture unit per sweaty minute scaled by regional moisture; outerwear uses a0.25 factor. Inactive clothing dries0.5 per minute. Every10 minutes at global perspiration50+, contacting regions at50+ can soil the affected garment:10% at50–74,25% at75–99,50% at100. The owner authorized implementing the previously proposed sweat rules; these probabilities are now runtime rules. Saved deterministic actor RNG and timestamps prevent rerolls on reload.

Sweat-soiled garments record a separate cause/affected-region entry. Existing urine-soiling, damage and other conditions are preserved; drying does not clear soiling. Player-owned and registered borrowed clothing, Priya’s actual worn household garments and Charity/Tits actual registered garments use existing item/condition records. This does not invent additional inventory for NPC outfits that lack individual item records.

**Shoes never receive sweat dirty/soiled tags or hamper eligibility.** Feet and footwear interiors may retain moisture for senses. Socks remain washable garments; shoes do not. Owned-shoe hamper validation also rejects already-worn shoes. Existing shared urine/other-fluid deposit rules are not reclassified as sweat.

## Infection boundary

Sweating alone creates neither contact nor ingestion nor infection. Regional state is available through a surface accessor, including last actual production time. Existing exposure thresholds remain unchanged. Tits’s typed saliva/sweat consumption triggers now use the actual regional surface accessor; see FLUID-CONTACT-INTERACTIONS.md.

# Post-mastery form tiers — approved rules and local implementation

## Owner correction and universal limits

Tiers advance inside a form's existing rarity. They do not promote Common to Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary, rewrite base rarity budgets or reprice the form. Initial mastery grants control and precedes tier advancement.

| Form rarity | Maximum post-mastery tier |
| --- | ---: |
| Common |0|
| Uncommon |1|
| Rare |2|
| Epic |3|
| Legendary |4|

The earlier assistant suggestion of absolute Tier 1=Uncommon/Tier 2=Rare/Tier 3=Epic/Tier 4=Legendary is withdrawn. An initially-Uncommon werewolf is unmastered with no tier upgrades earned. After initial mastery it remains Uncommon at tier 0 and can earn tier 1 only. HigherLegendary is a resource exception, not an automatically new tier or rarity cap.

## Approved rewards

Tier 1 awards two attribute bonus points, all to one selected stat or split. Tier 3 awards four additional points, likewise selected or split: six total attribute bonus points through tier 3. These are form-owned bonuses separate from its authored zero-to-ten base attributes, original player allocation and equipment. The existing effective-modifier pipeline permits bonuses beyond the base cap; the rarity's base budget remains unchanged.

Tiers 2 and 4 each grant a form-specific authored passive, a duration-limited continuous ability, or a single-use activation restricted by an authored cooldown. The form card must define the exact reward/effect, timing, conditions, costs, exclusions, interruption, reload state and actual activation/passive adapter. No universal damage/perk values or timing is supplied by this rule. An ability descriptor and a form-local grant adapter are supported by the shared controller; native effect/activation/timer controllers still need each actual ability's design and implementation. Registering an empty description is not a finished combat power.

## Local runtime

form-tiers.js supplies rarity limits, reward validation, ownership/mastery/out-of-combat gates, sequential advancement, exact stat distributions, stale-request prevention and atomic form-local grants. Native XP costs are approved and immutable: Tier 1 costs 500 XP, Tier 2 costs 1,000, Tier 3 costs 1,500, and Tier 4 costs 2,000. Each step is paid separately, for cumulative totals of 500 / 1,500 / 3,000 / 5,000. Eligible mastered forms may purchase attribute tiers. Ability tiers remain gated until the applicable actual form ability exists. Tests use the production XP costs and explicitly synthetic ability adapters, not invented authored powers.

Tier progression is saved on the actual owned form, with level and award receipts. Repeated requests cannot award/spend twice, invalid distributions/costs/ownership leave state unchanged, and grant adapters cannot rewrite protected base attributes/resources/rarity/identity/custody. Stat bonuses are derived from earned attribute-award receipts, not a raw legacy masteryTier number. Existing original-player stats, injuries/spending, rarity, mastery, inventory and money are preserved. Resource maxima/damage/cost tuning is not silently changed by these stat awards; the actual current effective-stat/roll pipeline is reused.

Equipment-region/current-stat/combat-snapshot consumers include earned form bonuses separately from base values. The Stats display identifies the tier modifier source. The Form panel shows current/max tier, current XP, next reward and the actual gating reason. XP assignment uses optional type-button controls without a nested form or unrelated required field, and shared text/menu actions call the same controller. Common forms cannot receive new tier XP assignments. Existing banked XP or legacy tier records are preserved for review; no silent refund, loss or reinterpretation is performed. XP can be banked on other owned unmastered forms, preserving the earlier allocation workflow; spending on an upgrade requires mastery.

Legacy nonzero tiers without the new award records require review, rather than receiving fabricated retrospective bonuses. Common legacy tier values never grant post-mastery upgrades. Conversion/resale must explicitly clear/reset the appropriate earned-tier state when those unbuilt services are authored; storage alone preserves it.

## Remaining design and integration

The owner rejected the earlier 150 / 300 / 600 / 1,200 proposal as too small for the game's scale. Approved and implemented: 500 / 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,000 XP per upgrade, with cumulative totals 500 / 1,500 / 3,000 / 5,000. No new XP income, automatic grant, retroactive spending or balance tuning is implied.

Owner defers individual tier 2/4 ability design until a Rare-or-higher form is being built. The learned-information observer recorded each visited location using two alternating descriptions/sources. Repeated observation treated these equivalent facts as revisions, retaining up to fifty false historical snapshots per location. Map exploration therefore inflated the saved character and the cost of copying/serializing it.

Both paths now record one canonical visit fact. A player-scoped migration collapses only repeated snapshots of the two known equivalent visit facts, retaining evidence sources, occurrence counts and timestamps. Distinct location history, NPC facts/corrections, visited tiles, appearance, forms, inventory and progress remain. Migration runs once per loaded guide object and can clean an older tab's repeated snapshots on a subsequent reload.

`rebuild/save-storage.js` provides the shared synchronous reader/writer for all three slots across Hub, both Title pages, Character Creation and the exported Title slot API. Existing JSON remains readable. Large saves, previously packed saves and smaller saves that hit quota use lossless UTF-16 packing when it reduces size. The envelope includes original length and a checksum. Corrupt packed data fails visibly rather than becoming an empty character. Reads return separate parsed objects; cached decode text never aliases mutable game state. Slot/status validation prevents wrong-slot writes without adding a new schema requirement to previously Hub-readable saves.

Atomic storage failures retain the last durable copy and the newest in-memory character. The Hub pauses automatic travel/live time and shows a blocking recovery dialog with Download current save and Retry saving. Timers cannot reload an older persisted copy over the dirty character. Download is available even under the sleep input guard. Character Creation uses the same recovery and does not navigate away after a failed confirmation write. No other slot, origin data or legacy key is deleted to make space. Backups are plain JSON, independent of the packed storage representation. A download preserves data; a new import workflow is outside this repair.

Packed slots require the updated client everywhere that reads them. The `EPI1LZ|` prefix deliberately fails legacy JSON parsing. A future release must ship the shared asset and every wired reader together. Older already-open pages should be closed after successful save/reload into the updated release; do not use an older build against a packed slot. An unpublished repair does not recover the current live tab: keep a tab with unsaved progress open and do not clear site storage.

## Travel responsiveness

Automatic travel no longer waits for descriptive AI prose. Pending action selection, NPC decisions and animal plans still block movement. Existing stale-result checks, focus/visibility pauses, cross-session ownership checks, 650ms step cadence and 8/12 game-minute travel costs remain. Intermediate planned-route steps keep their exact authored receipts without starting descriptions that would immediately become stale. Optional arrival prose may run when the narrator is free. Manual travel also avoids accumulating redundant narrator requests while that narrator is busy.

Every scene JSON serialized by `EpiAIContext.build` includes `tone`. Supported labels are `standard` (default), `suggestive` and `explicit_adult`. These are classifications, not permissions or instructions to add acts. Do not infer a label from player-supplied text or a physiological stat. The payload's existing `event` field describes only controller-resolved facts using concise neutral terminology. Observable actions, positions and body regions can be recorded where actually established. Keep attempts distinct from completed actions. A tone tag cannot establish consent, invent anatomy or produce a new physical outcome. Do not add coded directions for the external model to restore omitted acts. # Sleeping contact and regional drying — implemented locally, unpublished

## Detection and contact

`sleeping-contact.js` combines actual player/NPC sleep state, existing accepted direct-skin-contact sessions, unchanged body and co-location, and clothing barriers. Merely sharing a room, bed or sleep state never creates skin contact, permission or exposure. The existing household sleep/wake controller records real transitions; Erin’s actual form sleep and authored NPC sleep flags/activity are read directly. Unknown NPCs cannot inherit another actor’s sleep state.

Only the named pressed region dries at half speed; an explicitly known recipient region is also tracked. Hand-holding identifies both hand surfaces. “I keep my hand against Tits’s neck” identifies source neck and recipient hands. Source/recipient clothing prevents qualifying contact or breaks an existing contact. No new bed-sharing permission, private room, teleport or NPC acceptance policy is added.

Waking removes the half-speed factor. Separating, withdrawing, changing body, or inserting clothing ends the actual continuous exposure. Remaining moisture decays at the normal rate instead of disappearing instantly. All clocks persist and rendering/reload adds no elapsed time. Sleep pauses active kissing/consumption and accepted encounter exertion; a sleeping participant cannot answer a new request. An already accepted passive skin contact can continue.

## Math, in game minutes

For starting regional body-equivalent perspiration S>0, exposed drying duration is D=10+5×ceil(S/5). Pressed sleeping regions run their effective drying clock at0.5 minutes per actual game minute, so duration is2D, including the initial grace interval. Initially dry skin stays dry. Fresh-fluid lifetime remains120 game minutes; trapping moisture does not refresh its production timestamp or prolong infectiousness.

| Activity before rest | Score at stop | Exposed region dries after | Pressed sleeping region dries after | Intact-skin check after continued pressed contact |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|10 min|0|0|0|None|
|20 min|25|35 min|70 min|60 min after activity|
|30 min|35|45 min|90 min|60 min after activity|
|40 min|45|55 min|110 min|60 min after activity|
|50 min|55|65 min|130 min|60 min after activity|

These are initially dry neck-region calculations with no renewed exertion, nervousness or footwear enclosure. The50-minute case can remain damp beyond the fluid’s120-minute infectious lifetime. Actual qualifying thresholds remain60 continuous minutes for intact skin and30 for resolved broken skin at the recipient region. They trigger hidden resistance, not guaranteed infection. Separate-point rolls and stopping after infection are unchanged.

Reproduce the implemented calculation with `node scripts/calculate-sweat-drying.cjs`; evidence is `verification/sweat-transmission-math.json`.

Final local verification: **2,474 named cases across175 suites pass;30/30 phone-browser checks pass with zero browser errors**. Modified runtime/HTML script syntax and `git diff --check` pass. Evidence rollup:`work/travel-stage-repair/summary.json`; source hashes identify the tested local runtime. Paid model limitations above remain open.

# Relationship rollout coverage

The shared default is implemented for current and future human NPCs. This is not a claim that every character has a fully authored bespoke relationship tree or favorite-gift catalogue.

| --- | --- | --- |

| Tits | Purchase +1/item, kind remark +1, actual mistake patience +1, preferred gift +5 and incident reset; repeated disruptive touching/refusal rules | Shared meaningful conversation; her original actual gift controller remains authoritative |

| Future registered NPC | Character overrides remain possible | Generic defaults at the shared hearing boundary; authored interests/gifts via relationshipPolicy.interactionProfile |

Verification distinguishes layers: the focused suite covers every current human profile and a future registered actor, while native browser coverage exercises Priya’s date, typed/shortcut gifts, negatives, reloads and Erin’s gift. Native Tits/Charity/other NPC unit suites and Room D/fluid browser regressions also run. This does not claim paid-provider prose tests, or browser testing of every possible sentence for every NPC.

# Universal relationship interactions

## Current rule and implementation

Owner approved the conversation examples as the general template for all present and future NPCs, plus actual gifts suited to an NPC’s interests. The implementation uses the existing signed, stable-player/entity relationship record and event ledger, not another score. Generic defaults are inherited through relationship policies, heard speech is evaluated at the shared scene boundary, and existing direct dialogue paths use the same evaluator. Registered future NPCs inherit the generic exchanges automatically. Character-specific controllers and rewards remain authoritative.

| Resolved exchange | Default change |
| --- | ---: |
| Ask about an authored interest, then give a thoughtful relevant response | +2 |
| Share a relevant personal experience | +2 |
| Discuss media actually being shared | +2 |
| Express considerate kindness or appreciation | +2 |
| Give a specific sincere compliment | +1 |
| Dismiss or belittle something shared | −2 |
| Press after an actually stated boundary | −3 |
| Break an explicitly accepted recorded commitment | −2 |
| Transfer an actual preferred gift | +5 |

Preferred gifts reuse the established +5 preferred-gift reward. Tits’s gift controller still owns her transfer, +5, and touching-incident reset. Her purchase/kindness/patience rules remain separate. Erin’s existing care effects and quotas remain, without stacking the same shared exchange with another care award. Existing professional praise, listening, visits and aggression rules retain their own values and deduplication. Declining affection or an invitation is not a universal penalty.

## Context and repetition

Interest questions do not award points by themselves. Follow-ups require the same actual room and presentation. Shared-media credit requires an actual activity record and, for Priya’s date, the agreed identity. Positive categories resolve one at a time; repeating or paraphrasing a category for the same topic in the current date/day does not produce more credit. The date has its own scope; ordinary interactions use a game-day scope. Existing character-specific cooldowns remain separate.

Private thoughts, hypotheticals, reported insults, unavailable recipients and bodies unable to speak do not qualify for these spoken exchanges. Negated dismissal is not an insult. Existing NPC agreement, access, recognition and body rules do not change. Eve can receive appropriate actual remote conversation, but has no physical gift-receiving body. Dart retains his authored care/play/handling rules rather than being assigned human film conversation.

Actual authored NPC replies can record a stated boundary; generated prose cannot create penalties or awards. Commitment outcomes require an accepted controller record. Priya’s accepted after-work invitation is connected to completion/missed attendance; merely declining an offer or leaving unfinished unaccepted content does not create a promise penalty. Other controllers can call the same accepted/completed/broken adapter where an actual commitment exists.

## Gifts and authored interests

Typed “I give {owned item} to {person}” and the optional gift shortcut share one controller. The item must exist, be carried, owned and unequipped. Borrowed, quest/bound/cursed/form items cannot be transferred through the generic path. A declined/unmatched gift stays with the player. A transfer removes one unit, preserves any remaining stack’s ownership, stores the recipient’s actual item and receipt, and awards once per transfer ID across reloads.

Current authored profiles include Priya’s crystals/writing/rom-coms, Erin’s foxes/books/plants, Tits’s pink/sparkly interests and nightlife/sweets, Charity’s stories/mending/crosswords/roses, Daniel’s cooking/hiking/wine, Nadia’s creative marketing and Richard’s department/business interests. Preferred-gift matching is configured only where a preference is authored: Priya crystals, Erin fox items, Charity roses/mint chocolate chip, Daniel wine from his established wine-collecting interest, and Tits’s existing preferred-gift rules. No missing personal gift preference was invented for another NPC. Erin’s gift is stored with her existing form state; no second physical Erin is spawned.

Future NPCs can provide `relationshipPolicy.interactionProfile` with `interests: {topic: [aliases]}` and `gifts: [authored preference phrases]`. Their policy can override a default event weight. Registering a new interest does not reveal it to the player; existing learned-information rules remain separate. The recognizer supports contextual common phrases, not unrestricted semantic understanding of every possible sentence.

## Player access and verification

Eve’s live lexicon explains relationship conversation, gifts and repetition. The relationship display includes recent recorded score changes. Priya’s listening shortcut now has a matching “I listen to Priya” text route. A real typed date conversation can reach +10; her offered kiss waits until the thirty-minute shared date finishes; no developer score mutation is used in that browser scenario.

Focused tests cover the date threshold, distinct categories, repetition/paraphrases, media context, private/hypothetical speech, presence/body/presentation changes, negatives, accepted commitments, gifts/ownership/stacks/quest restrictions, Erin, future registered NPCs and player isolation. Browser checks cover the actual composer, clock, text/shortcut gift parity, negatives and reloads. See verification/universal-relationships-summary.json for the final evidence. No owner saves or paid model calls were used. This follow-up is local and unpublished; v1.0.130 remains unchanged.
